intended_object: The set of defining equations of the symplectic group scheme Sp_{2m} inside GL_{2m} over a commutative ring R: the entries of X J_m X^T − J_m in the coordinate ring O(GL_{2m}), where X is the generic matrix and J_m is the standard alternating form. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the library's use of the set as generators of the defining Hopf ideal.
explanation: The definition is an abbreviation for ConstantForm.relationSet R (m+m) (JFin m R). That set is the range of (i, j) ↦ relationMatrix i j, where relationMatrix = genericMatrix * C.map algebraMap * genericMatrixᵀ − C.map algebraMap, i.e. X C Xᵀ − C. JFin m R is Mathlib's standard alternating form Matrix.J (Fin m) R, reindexed to Fin (m+m) coordinates along finSumFinEquiv. So the set is exactly the entries of X J_m Xᵀ − J_m in O(GL_{2m}), the standard defining equations of Sp_{2m} (Milne, §2.3 and §24.6). The library spans an ideal by these entries to cut out the subgroup scheme. It works over an arbitrary commutative ring, which is the natural base for group schemes. The size 2m is built into the symplectic group, and indexing by Fin (m+m) matches the library's GL(n) coordinate Hopf algebra without losing generality. The construction for an arbitrary constant form C is already available separately (ConstantForm), so this specialization is not too narrow. I did not search Mathlib for a counterpart: Mathlib has Matrix.J and the symplectic group of matrices over a ring, but those concern points, and I am not aware of a scheme-level symplectic group or a set of its defining equations there. One could argue that a generating set for an ideal is only a presentation device (not_a_mathematical_object); I chose faithful because "the defining equations" is a standard notion in the literature.
